subject: Re: On-Prem Standing Wave — Throughput Collapse, Escalation & Next Steps
messages:
From: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@oakhaborlabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@oakhaborlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 03:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput collapse on our on-prem cluster — urgent

Vanessa / Redwood team,

We woke up to a sustained throughput drop in our private deployment (VPC-connected on-prem cluster) starting ~01:30 UTC. p95 increased from ~120ms to 2.1s and sustained token throughput collapsed by ~68%. We also see a rise in 500s for the inference API during the highest-concurrency windows. Attached is a screenshot of the per-shard QPS and a KV cache hit-rate dump from last night.

Quick facts:
- Cluster: OHL-prod-3 (16 x A100 equivalent) running Redwood private 1.9.2
- Model: open-llama-70b-int8-merged (pinned)
- First observed: 2027-04-20 01:28:00 UTC
- Impact: production traffic degraded for 3 of 6 customer-facing routes; revenue-impacting.

We need immediate remediation guidance and a plan to stabilize. Our SRE is standing by but asked for Redwood's ops playbook and whether a fast rollback to 1.9.1 would help. Also need an exec-level contact for contractual/credits conversation if this persists.

Thanks,
Sarah
Head of Platform, Oak Harbor Labs

Attachments referenced: oakhb-deploy-metrics-20270420.png, kvcache-dump-20270420.json
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@oakhaborlabs.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@oakhaborlabs.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 04:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse on our on-prem cluster — urgent

Sarah — thanks for the flag and the attachments. I understand the impact and am escalating immediately. Short answers first:
- We have an on-call runbook for private deploy regressions; I'll share the playbook and a recommended quick rollback path.
- Rolling to 1.9.1 may help if the regression is runtime/kernel-related, but we should confirm root cause before a full rollback; a canary rollback for 2 of 16 nodes is safer.
- Exec support: looping in Laura and Marissa to surface ops/resourcing and to coordinate a leadership sync.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm whether you observed increased prefetch/memory pressure on the host during the window? (nvtop/dmesg outputs)
2) Please confirm traffic routing — were requests evenly balanced across shards or did your HA layer shift load?

We will:
- Kick off an ops runbook (Marissa) and produce a short remediation playbook in the next 90 minutes.
- Run a quick hotfix test (KV cache invalidation + per-shard soft-restart) on a canary set.

I'll set an internal exec sync and share an external timeline for Oak Harbor within 2 hours.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@oakhaborlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 06:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse on our on-prem cluster — urgent

Thanks Vanessa / Sarah — did an initial triage against the artifacts. Key observations:
- The KV cache hit-rate in the attached dump dropped from ~83% to ~12% during the window; cache population appears to have been evicted rapidly.
- We see a correlated spike in per-token decode retries around the same timestamp (our tracer shows many short-lived attempts to rewarm K/V segments).
- One kernel log line showed a recoverable cuCtx synchronization stall on two GPUs; that can manifest as cascading latency and backlog if the request fanout is high.

Hypothesis (early): a workload shift increased prefix diversity + a small regression in our JIT/kernel selection in 1.9.2 leading to KV cache fragmentation under the current batching config. That combination would cause higher per-token compute and lower effective throughput.

Short remediation steps I can run now (will need Marissa to coordinate rolling restarts):
1) Invalidate KV cache and force a rewarm on canary nodes (2 nodes, off-peak routing).
2) Temporarily reduce max_batch_size and increase batching time window to favour more stable kernels (config tweak, no deploy).
3) If canary stabilizes, roll the config cluster-wide and schedule a controlled quantization/kernel-resolve rollback if required.

I will attach a minimal playbook and the exact CLI commands in a follow-up.

Laura
Sr. Eng, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@oakhaborlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse on our on-prem cluster — urgent

Team — I executed the canary plan at 07:40 UTC: invalidated KV cache and soft-restarted the serving process on 2 nodes (node-05 and node-07). Results:
- Node canary p95 recovered from ~1.9s to ~140ms within 16 minutes as the KV cache re-populated.
- Overall cluster throughput improved by ~22% but not to baseline; the remaining gap correlates with a persistent higher decode CPU on other nodes.
- No new 500s observed on the canary nodes post intervention.

Next ops steps proposed (safe sequence):
A) Roll soft-restart + rewarm across the remaining nodes in rolling fashion (4 nodes at once during low-traffic windows).
B) Apply temporary serving config: max_batch_size -10%, batching_window +30ms. This is a config change (no build).
C) Schedule a kernel-selection audit to identify why 1.9.2 picked a less-predictable kernel under these prefixes.

Impact/risks: rolling restarts will temporarily shift traffic and increase request latency on the restarted nodes for ~8-20 minutes each. We recommend executing B before C.

Attachments: private-playbook-v1.docx (ops checklist and CLI commands)

Marissa
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@oakhaborlabs.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse on our on-prem cluster — urgent

Vanessa / Team — copying leadership and ops checklist notes. Two asks that need exec signoff from Redwood:
1) Offer immediate commercial remediation (service credit or one-time dedicated engineering hours) to Oak Harbor Labs given production impact. Need approval to offer up to 5% credit or a 10-hour engineering retainer at no charge.
2) Approve an expedited kernel rollback window for 1.9.2 -> 1.9.1 across OHL-prod-3 if audit shows kernel-selection regression. This is higher risk and needs a leadership ok for a scheduled maintenance window (we propose 2027-04-24 02:00 UTC).

Sarah — what remedy would be most helpful from your side (credit vs. engineering hours)? We want to make a good-faith operational offer while we finish root-cause.

-Aditya
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@oakhaborlabs.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-Prem Standing Wave — Throughput Collapse, Escalation & Next Steps

Sarah — summary and decisions after internal exec review: 
1) Immediate stabilization: Marissa's rolling KV rewarm + temporary serving config will proceed tonight during your low-traffic window (2027-04-24 02:00 UTC). Marissa will own coordination.
2) Canary rollback: We will not do a full rollback pre-audit. Laura will run a kernel-selection audit in the next 12 hours; if it definitively points to 1.9.2 regression we will schedule a controlled rollback during a second-maintenance window (candidate 2027-04-25 02:00 UTC).
3) Commercial remediation: Redwood will provide Oak Harbor Labs 10 hours of prioritized engineering time to help tune their private deployment and run a joint post-mortem. If the audit points to a Redwood code regression, we will also issue a 5% one-time service credit. Aditya will coordinate the credit/contract paperwork.

External exec touchpoint: I will be available for a 30-minute call with your CTO at 14:00 UTC today if you want to escalate to exec-level; Hannah will send a calendar invite.

Open items:
- Sarah: confirm acceptance of our remediation offer and your preferred time for the 30m exec call.
- Oak Harbor: share any additional host-level logs (dmesg, nvtop) if available to speed audit.

We will attach the ops playbook and the quick CLI checklist (private-playbook-v1.docx) to the HubSpot deal record and share Slack channel access for the joint incident.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
